{{Short description|Australian computer scientist (1933–2004)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}

''For other uses, see [[Chris Wallace (disambiguation)]].''
{{more footnotes needed|date=February 2013}}
'''Christopher Stewart Wallace''' (26 October 1933{{snd}}7 August 2004) was an Australian [[computer scientist]] and [[physicist]].

Wallace is notable for having devised:
* The [[minimum message length]] principle<ref>{{cite journal |title=An Information Measure for Classification |first1=C. S. |last1=Wallace |first2=D. M. |last2=Boulton |journal=The Computer Journal |volume=11 |issue=2 |date=August 1968 |pages=185–194 |doi=10.1093/comjnl/11.2.185 |url=http://www.allisons.org/ll/MML/Structured/1968-WB-CJ/|doi-access=free }}</ref> &mdash; an [[information theory|information-theoretic]] principle in [[statistics]], [[econometrics]], [[machine learning]], [[inductive inference]] and [[knowledge discovery]] which can be seen both as a mathematical formalisation of [[Occam's Razor]] and as an invariant [[Bayesian inference|Bayesian]] method of model selection and [[point estimation]],
* The [[Wallace tree]] form of [[binary multiplier]] (1964),
* a variety of random number generators,<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://maths-people.anu.edu.au/~brent/pd/rpb213.pdf |title=Some Comments on C. S. Wallace's Random Number Generators |first=Richard P. |last=Brent |journal=The Computer Journal |volume=51 |issue=5 |date=September 2008 |pages=579–584 |doi=10.1093/comjnl/bxm122|arxiv=1005.2314 |s2cid=16287927 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.datamining.monash.edu.au/software/random |title=MDMC Software - Random Number Generators |website=Monash Data Mining Centre |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130722135627/http://www.datamining.monash.edu.au/software/random/ |archivedate=2013-07-22 }}</ref>
* a theory in physics and philosophy that [[entropy]] is not the arrow of time,
* a refrigeration system (from the 1950s, whose design is still in use in 2010),
* hardware for detecting and counting cosmic rays,
* design of computer operating systems,
* the notion of [[universality probability]] in mathematical logic,
* and a vast range of other works - see, e.g., {{cite journal |title=Christopher Stewart WALLACE (1933-2004) memorial special issue |journal=Computer Journal |volume=51 |issue=5 |pages=523–607 |date=5 September 2008 |doi=10.1093/comjnl/bxm117}} and its ''[http://www.csse.monash.edu.au/~dld/Publications/2008/DLDowe_ForewordReCSWallace_CompJVol51Num5Sept2008pp523-560.pdf Foreword re C. S. Wallace ]'', pp [http://www.csse.monash.edu.au/~dld/Publications/2008/DLDowe_ForewordReCSWallace_CompJVol51Num5Sept2008pp523-560.pdf 523-560].

He was appointed Foundation Chair of Information Science at [[Monash University]] in 1968 at the age of 34 (before the Department was re-named Computer Science), and Professor Emeritus in 1996. Wallace was a fellow of the [[Australian Computer Society]] and in 1995 he was appointed a fellow of the [[Association for Computing Machinery|ACM]] "For research in a number of areas in Computer Science including fast multiplication algorithm, minimum message length principle and its applications, random number generation, computer architecture, numerical solution of ODE's, and contribution to Australian Computer Science."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://fellows.acm.org/fellow_citation.cfm?id=1058015&srt=alpha&alpha=W |title=ACM Fellows: Chris S Wallace |website=Association for Computing Machinery |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060819085526/http://fellows.acm.org/fellow_citation.cfm?id=1058015&srt=alpha&alpha=W |archive-date=19 August 2006}}</ref>

Wallace received his PhD (in Physics) from the [[University of Sydney]] in 1959. He was married to Judy Ogilvie, the first secretary and programme librarian of [[SILLIAC]], which was launched on the 12 of September 1956 at the University of Sydney and which was one of Australia's first computers.<ref>{{cite news |title=Love at First Byte |first=Marie |last=Jacobs |url=http://www.usyd.edu.au/alumni/activities/magazine/winter06/byte.shtml |work=Sydney Alumni Magazine |date=Winter 2006 |publisher=University of Sydney |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060825111548/http://www.usyd.edu.au/alumni/activities/magazine/winter06/byte.shtml |archive-date=25 August 2006}}</ref> He also engineered one of the world's first Local Area Networks in the mid-1960s.<ref>{{cite journal |url=http://www.cs.man.ac.uk/CCS/res/res19.htm#k |title=Letters to the Editor |first=John M. |last=Bennett |journal=Resurrection: The Bulletin of the Computer Conservation Society |issue=19 |date=Spring 1998}}</ref>
